newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Danish PM says sees no need for early EMU vote.
newsitem.headline: Danish PM says sees no need for early EMU vote.

text.p: Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said on Thursday he saw no need to call an early referendum on joining a single European currency.
"At the moment I see no reason to ask the Danish people to vote in a referendum," Rasmussen told a news conference during a one-day forum on the future single European currency.
Danes voted in a 1993 referendum to endorse the Maastricht treaty on condition that Denmark did not join European Economic and Monetary Union.

"We fulfil all five Maastricht criteria but we do not want to join (a single currency). I say to the Danish people, I respect your decision and it will not be changed until the situation alters," Rasmussen said.
But he insisted that Denmark's commitment to the convergence criteria was unshaken.
"Irrespective of EMU, fulfilment of the convergence criteria is...a sound principle for the conduct of economic policy for sustained economic growth and increased employment," he said in a speech.
The Danish prime minister argued that member states should do more to tackle the Europe-wide problem of unemployment and warned that EMU did not have all the answers.

"EMU does not solve all problems. Sustained strong economic growth should be combined with more effective domestic labour market reforms...and economic policy coordination among EU member states," Rasmussen said.
He also encouraged the European Union to establish an exchange rate mechanism that would avoid rifts between those countries participating in a single currency and those outside.
"EMU is not only a question for the 'ins', it is also a question for the 'outs'," he said. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
